frase_gancho.texto: A house of quarried stone and stained glass where Mario Moreno came to rest, and a pool with a mosaic by Diego Rivera.

puente_narrativo.texto: This house brings the Cuernavaca tour to an end: here you can stay in the garden or walk back to the center.

Mario Moreno, Cantinflas, was one of the great comedians of Mexico, and this house in Cuernavaca was his retreat for rest. He acquired it around the 1950s. It is a two-story house in the neocolonial style, with quarried stone walls, stained glass windows and gardens. Today it works as a house museum. It has art galleries with works from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries and photographs of Cantinflas with his friends. guion_largo.texto:
This stop is optional: the house is not always open, and you never know when it will be. Mario Moreno was born in nineteen eleven and died in nineteen ninety-three. Under the name Cantinflas, he became one of the most beloved actors in Mexico and the Spanish-speaking world. His way of talking, tangled and full of twists and turns, gave rise to a verb: cantinflear. And his most famous line, “ahí está el detalle,” is still in use today.

This house is at number one hundred two Benito Juárez Boulevard, in downtown Cuernavaca. It was one of several residences Cantinflas owned. He acquired it around the 1950s and used it as a personal retreat. It is said that he finished writing the script of El señor fotógrafo here, in nineteen fifty-three. Among his visitors, María Félix is mentioned, along with other figures from the golden age of cinema.

Later the house almost fell into oblivion. It was restored with an effort to preserve its original character. A press release from two thousand twenty-six describes it as a two-story property in the Mexican neocolonial style, with quarried stone walls, stained glass windows and abundant gardens. Sources disagree on when it opened as a museum: two thousand twenty-one or two thousand twenty-three. It is known as Cassa Gaia.

The detail that will most interest those coming from seeing the art of the center is at the pool. There is a Venetian glass mosaic there made by Diego Rivera, who was a close friend of Cantinflas. According to one report, it represents the tree of life of Gaia, the goddess of fertility. That same report says the signature refers to Frida Kahlo, with a toad, because she called Rivera the toad. This is a press description, not an official catalog entry. What matters is that it is a mosaic by a famous muralist, made for a private pool.

There are also art galleries. According to the reports, there are ten rooms with works by artists of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Some are devoted to the movement called Ruptura, which emerged in Mexico in the 1950s. There are also photographs of Cantinflas with his friends, and a space dedicated to him.

If the house is open, take your time to view the pool from different angles. A mosaic under water changes with the light and with the movement of the person looking at it. Also ask whether the tour includes the gardens.

If you find the door closed, you lose nothing of the tour: you can end at the Jardín Borda. According to the press reports, admission is free. Hours change; check the Before You Go section.

A vacation home tells things that a museum does not. Here you can see the preferences of someone who spent half his life making other people laugh: the light, the gardens, the water of the pool. And Rivera’s presence is a reminder that the great figures of Mexican art and film knew one another, visited one another and gave each other works.

Close the tour calmly. That is the idea of this tour: Cuernavaca is layers of power, faith and rest. Tlahuicas, Franciscans, miners, emperors, muralists and comedians. All of them fit within a few streets.

texto: Find the pool and the Diego Rivera mosaic, and notice the colors of the glass
Look at the stained glass windows and the quarried stone walls, and imagine what life here was like in the 1950s
If there are photographs of Cantinflas, find one with his friends and try to recognize someone

texto.Style: Mexican neocolonial, two stories, quarried stone and stained glass
texto.Work by Diego Rivera: Venetian glass mosaic at the pool

texto.pregunta: Myth: Cantinflas only lived in Mexico City.
texto.respuesta: Reality: He had several houses. This one, in Cuernavaca, was his retreat for rest from the 1950s on.
